title: Quantitative Criteria and Considerations in Cost-Benefit Analysis for Rationalisation of Bus Routes
what_it_is: Quantitative Criteria and Considerations in Cost-Benefit Analysis for Rationalisation of Bus Routes

sections.label: Bus route rationalisation criteria
sections.summary: Minister for Transport was asked whether LTA uses quantitative criteria and cost-benefit analyses for bus route rationalisation, including intangible factors.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song
sentences.text: asked the Minister for Transport on the rationalisation of bus routes (a) whether LTA applies quantitative criteria and conducts quantitative cost-benefit analyses; (b) if yes, what quantitative criteria are applied and what are the factors taken into account in the cost-benefit analysis; and (c) how are intangible factors, such as certain buses providing a less crowded alternative to trains, taken into consideration.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
sentences.text: This includes a subsidy of around $1 billion for trains and another $1 billion for buses.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
sentences.text: To keep our public transport system sustainable for all stakeholders, we had previously explained in this House that it is important to strike a balance between providing convenience for commuters and keeping the overall costs affordable for commuters and taxpayers.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
sentences.text: This includes making changes to some of the existing bus services which run parallel to new Mass Rapid Transit (MRT) lines and have experienced significant reductions in their ridership levels when more commuters switch to taking the MRT.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
sentences.text: These assessments are done on a case-by-case basis, taking into account commuter travel patterns and the overall connectivity and resilience of our public transport network.

sections.label: Deciding which parallel buses change
sections.summary: Not all buses parallel to new MRT lines are removed; decisions on retaining, changing, shortening or removing them are based on commuter travel pattern changes.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
sentences.text: So, we do not take away all existing bus services that run parallel to the new MRT lines.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
sentences.text: But in deciding which ones to retain and which ones to change, shorten or remove, these decisions would then have to be also based on the changes in commuter travel patterns.

sections.label: Bedok Reservoir Bus 228 frequency
sections.summary: In Bedok Reservoir several buses were removed, and the member's focus was increasing frequency of remaining Bus 228, a live constituent issue.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song
sentences.text: In fact, if the Minister has tracked the arguments I have made about this issue in the past two years, in my area in Bedok Reservoir, several buses were removed.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song
sentences.text: I do not recall calling for the buses to be restored.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song
sentences.text: But my focus was always on increasing the frequency of the remaining bus, which is Bus 228, which is still a live issue with my constituents because whenever I go down to the constituency, it is a very common feedback I get that the frequency of the bus is not enough and, because of that, they call for the bringing back of the other buses that were taken away.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song
sentences.text: But my argument to the Government has always been to increase the frequency of Bus 228.

sections.label: Keeping some parallel bus routes
sections.summary: Some bus routes parallel to MRT lines are deliberately kept because different commuters need different options, but adjustments are needed as resources are finite.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
sentences.text: In fact, we deliberately, as I have explained, maintain and keep some of the bus routes that run parallel to MRT lines precisely because they are different commuters who require different options.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
sentences.text: But at the same time, we need to make some adjustments because the resources are finite and we do not want to have a situation where we just keep adding new bus services and new bus routes without actually reallocating some of the existing ones which have seen a drop in ridership levels.
